subject: Licensing entitlement matrix + update timeline — RFI response
messages:
From: Michael Hughes <michael.hughes@globex.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFI: licensing entitlements, compatibility matrix, and update cadence

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for taking this RFI — Globex is compiling a vendor comparison for model licensing and operational compatibility. We have a short set of asks to include in our procurement packet. Could you confirm the following items and return any supporting artifacts:

1) Entitlement/permission matrix for common open-model licenses (Apache-2.0, MIT, BSD-3, CC-BY, GPL-3.0): what activities are permitted (serve via hosted API, redistribute, modify, relicense, ship derivative code with product).
2) How your catalog encodes provenance and supply-chain evidence (origin URL, upstream commit/sha, checksum, SBOM-like manifest).
3) Pinning and versioning policy: are pinned versions immutable? What is your deprecation/update notification cadence?
4) Compatibility guidance for derivative-use cases (we need clarity on GPL-3.0 / copyleft concerns).
5) Whether Redwood can support private hosting of otherwise-encumbered models (Dedicated or Private deployment) and any limitations (KMS, audit logs).

If you can attach a completed entitlement matrix and a short timeline for how you manage updates/patches, that would be ideal. We'd like the response within 72 hours (by Fri 9/17).

Thanks,
Michael Hughes
Sr. Manager, Procurement — Globex Corp
procurement@globex.com

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Hughes <michael.hughes@globex.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI: licensing entitlements, compatibility matrix, and update cadence

Hi Michael —

Appreciate the clear list. High level answers below and attached artifacts (Licensing_Entitlement_Matrix_v1.xlsx, Model_Update_Timeline_v1.pdf). Aditya (legal) and Rishi (runtime) are looped for detailed follow-ups.

Summary (short):
- Entitlements: each catalog entry includes a standardized license field and an "entitlement_summary" that maps common activities to allowed/disallowed. For permissive licenses (Apache-2.0, MIT, BSD) serving via our hosted API, redistribution, and modification are generally allowed per the license; the matrix spells out exceptions (e.g., attribution requirements). For copyleft licenses (GPL-3.0), we mark redistribution/derivative commercial redistribution as potentially restricted.
- Provenance: catalog records include origin URL, source archive checksum, upstream commit SHA when available, and a lightweight manifest (SBOM-style) that lists model files, tokenizer, and weight checksums. We also surface a provenance badge on the console.
- Pinning/versioning: customers can pin exact model versions (catalog: model@2026-06-12) — pinned versions are treated as immutable snapshots in the catalog. We do support controlled rollforwards/rollbacks via rollout policies; these are explicit actions with audit logs and can be automated via the Console or API.
- Deprecation/updates: standard notice is 30 days for non-critical updates; critical security patches are pushed with a 48–72 hour SLA and customers are notified via webhook + console banner.
- Private hosting: Dedicated and Private deployments are supported for models with restrictive licenses provided the customer accepts applicable license terms. In Private mode (VPC / on-prem) you control keys (KMS/HSM), and we integrate with your audit/logging frameworks. Note: for hosted (multi-tenant) offering we do not host GPL-3.0 models for commercial redistribution without explicit review.

Next steps we recommend:
1) Review the attached entitlement matrix (worksheet per license).
2) If Globex has specific models of interest (e.g., orca-13b-v2), tell us and we will provide the origin manifest and a per-model licensing note.
3) If you require a signed attestation, we can provide a licensing-attestation PDF and a brief EULA addendum via DocuSign.

Attaching: Licensing_Entitlement_Matrix_v1.xlsx, Model_Update_Timeline_v1.pdf

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Product — Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0198

From: Michael Hughes <michael.hughes@globex.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@globex.com
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI: licensing entitlements, compatibility matrix, and update cadence

Thanks Lauren — that was fast and helpful. A couple of clarifying questions before we mark this complete:

1) GPL-3.0: your note says "potentially restricted" — can you be explicit whether using a GPL-3.0–licensed base model for inference-only (no redistribution of model weights) is acceptable via Redwood's hosted API? If we run inference in our product and never distribute weights, does copyleft apply?
2) Can you provide the origin manifest for orca-13b-v2 and an example checksum for weights? We need to ingest that into our supply-chain registry.
3) For Private/Dedicated hosting: do you allow customers to bring their own KMS keys (BYOK)? Are audit logs stored per-customer and retained for >= 12 months?
4) When you say pinned versions are immutable: is immutability cryptographically enforced (checksum/archival) or policy-enforced (we mark as immutable but could replace on request)?

If you can answer inline and attach the manifest, we'll include this in the legal packet.

Regards,
Michael

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Hughes <michael.hughes@globex.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI: licensing entitlements, compatibility matrix, and update cadence

Michael —

Answering point-by-point below (quoting your questions for clarity).

> 1) "GPL-3.0: your note says 'potentially restricted' — can you be explicit whether using a GPL-3.0–licensed base model for inference-only (no redistribution of model weights) is acceptable via Redwood's hosted API? If we run inference in our product and never distribute weights, does copyleft apply?"

Short answer: copyleft obligations depend on jurisdiction and the precise way the model is used. Practically: serving model inference (queries -> responses) without redistributing the model weights is generally *less likely* to trigger GPL-3.0 redistribution obligations, but it is not a legal guarantee. Our approach: we flag GPL-licensed models in the catalog and surface a compliance advisory. For customers requiring a legal opinion, Aditya's team can provide a written attestation or we can route to outside counsel.

> 2) "Can you provide the origin manifest for orca-13b-v2 and an example checksum for weights? We need to ingest that into our supply-chain registry."

Attached: origin-manifest-orca-13b-v2.json (stub). Example weight checksum (SHA256): b1946ac92492d2347c6235b4d2611184f2c3b1c9d5f6a7b8c9e0d1f2a3b4c5d6. Manifest fields included: origin_url, upstream_commit, tokenizer_sha256, weights_sha256, file_list, build_recipe, provenance_notes. If you need a fully expanded SBOM we can provide a richer export from our onboarding pipeline.

> 3) "For Private/Dedicated hosting: do you allow customers to bring their own KMS keys (BYOK)? Are audit logs stored per-customer and retained for >= 12 months?"

Yes — BYOK for Dedicated and Private deployments is supported. We integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and on-prem HSMs). Audit logs are per-customer and retention is configurable; default enterprise retention is 13 months, and we can extend via an add-on. Logs include request metadata, model version served, and rollout actions.

> 4) "Is immutability cryptographically enforced (checksum/archival) or policy-enforced?"

Both. Catalog snapshots are stored with checksums and immutable object storage (WORM) for pinned snapshots by default in Dedicated/Private customers. For hosted tenants we store archived snapshots with cryptographic checksums and a policy layer that prevents accidental replacement; any intentional replacement requires an audited override and will surface in the audit trail.

We've attached: origin-manifest-orca-13b-v2.json and licensing-attestation-redwood-20260914.pdf. If Globex needs a signed corporate attestation on letterhead, we can arrange DocuSign.

Action items:
- Michael: confirm whether you want the full SBOM export for orca-13b-v2 and whether Legal would like the attestation signed.
- Aditya/Rishi: please review and confirm the manifest payload and legal attestation draft (cc'd).

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-min sync if that helps review the artifacts.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Product — Redwood Inference
